Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill at Second Reading

Second Reading7 April 2026 – 8 April 2026 bill-789, bill-790, bill-791

A Bill at Second Reading that extends Minimum Energy Performance Standards and the Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme to regulated goods imported by end users for their own use, and empowers the Minister to make regulations for online platforms to remove non-compliant listings.

From 1 July 2026, end users importing regulated goods for their own use are to register with NEA, meet MEPS and carry MELS labels, with fines up to $10,000 per import for non-compliance. Registration and renewal fees for end users are to be waived, and existing schemes such as the Energy Efficiency Grant and Climate Vouchers are cited as support. The Bill excludes second-hand or used regulated goods and regulated lamps.

What happens next The Senior Minister of State said the new regulations are intended to take effect from 1 July 2026; the transcript does not record a vote or later stage.

Open questions from this debate (19)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • How many regulated goods are currently imported for own use, and what is their total annual energy consumption?
  • What is the projected reduction in energy consumption if all F&B businesses deploy MEPS- and MELS-compliant appliances?
  • How will NEA enforce the requirement for goods arriving by post, courier, land checkpoints, or checked baggage?
  • Will there be a transition period or fee support for SMEs, consumers and first-time applicants?
  • How will the Bill treat individuals who later sell an imported appliance on peer-to-peer platforms?
  • Will software-driven energy degradation after registration be regulated, and how?
  • Will lighting be included in the own-use import regime, and on what timeline?
  • Will waivers and Director-General decisions be published or reported in aggregated form?
  • Will online platforms be required to screen listings before they appear, and what consumer protections apply after payment?
  • Will the Energy Efficiency Grant be expanded to cover all regulated goods?
  • Will there be top-ups to the Climate Friendly Households Programme for lower-income families?
  • Will there be a shared product registry or simplified pathway for subsequent importers?
  • Will there be an interagency coordination framework and a single point of contact for importers?
  • Will there be public reporting to Parliament on waivers, appeals and enforcement trends?
  • Will there be a priority processing lane for SMEs with high-efficiency products?
  • What is the projected cost impact on households and SMEs?
  • Will compliant models remain competitively priced?
  • How will NEA distinguish deliberate circumvention from genuine misunderstanding?
  • Will registration of goods be retrospectively revoked if a software update degrades performance?

Veterinary Practice Bill at Second Reading, creating a Veterinary Council to register and discipline vets

Second Reading8 April 2026 bill-792

A Bill at Second Reading, moved by the Minister of State for National Development on behalf of the Minister for National Development, that establishes a Veterinary Council to register veterinarians and regulate the practice of veterinary medicine in Singapore.

The Minister said vets will have to be registered with the new Council and hold a valid practising certificate to practise, and that the Registrar must publish registered vets' particulars so the public can search for and verify a vet's registration status and place of practice. The maximum financial penalty for unlawful practice or misrepresentation as a vet rises from $10,000 to $50,000. Existing AVS-licensed vets will be temporarily deemed duly qualified and must obtain registration and a practising certificate within a stipulated grace period to continue practising.

    • Mr Alvin Tan said pet ownership is a personal choice and a long-term commitment, and encouraged prospective owners to consider the full cost of raising a pet.

    • Mr Alvin Tan said AVS and the Council will partner MOE and the Institutes of Higher Learning to strengthen veterinary-related education and training locally, including for mid-career entrants.

    • Mr Alvin Tan said the Council is first and foremost a regulator whose primary duty is to maintain professional standards.

      The Veterinary Council President and members are appointed by the Minister, who can also remove members where necessary.

    • Mr Alvin Tan said the Government will continue to engage the vet sector before developing the regulatory framework for vet nurses.

    • Mr Alvin Tan said there is no change to the existing 12-month maximum imprisonment term.

What happens next The Minister said the Bill will commence in two stages: establishing the Veterinary Council this year, followed by the remaining provisions including the registration regime and disciplinary framework for vets next year. The transcript does not record the next parliamentary step after the Second Reading debate.

Open questions from this debate (10)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • Whether a locally offered veterinary degree programme will be introduced, and on what timeline.
  • Whether regulation will be extended to pet groomers and dog trainers, and when.
  • What the prescribed conditions and supervision arrangements for non-vets, including community caregivers, will say in practice.
  • Whether a transition period will apply to enforcement against community animal caregivers performing basic first aid.
  • Whether the exemption power under clause 86 will be used to carve out community animal welfare activities.
  • Whether fee benchmarks, itemised billing or mandatory fee disclosures will be introduced, and when.
  • What the registration and practising certificate fees will be.
  • How many investigators will be appointed and whether a dedicated enforcement unit will be set up.
  • Whether Industry Abuse Protections will be extended to veterinarians.
  • Whether an ITE pathway into veterinary or animal care work will be developed.

Adjournment Motion on developing a low-altitude economy and eVTOL industry in Singapore

Adjournment Motion8 April 2026 matter-adj-2959

An Adjournment Motion debate in which Dr Neo Kok Beng set out opportunities and proposals for a low-altitude economy and eVTOL industry, and Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling responded on the Government’s approach.

The transcript says drones are already used in Singapore for tasks such as ship-to-shore deliveries, tunnel and façade inspections, high-rise ledge cleaning and crowd monitoring, and that using drones for reservoir monitoring can potentially reduce required man-hours by up to 70%. It also says eVTOLs may not be viable extensively as a domestic transport option in Singapore, but could eventually be viable for cross-border travel to adjacent offshore islands or cross-border cargo transfer.

  • Dr Neo Kok Beng

    • Dr Neo declared that he is the founder of an eVTOL company that designs manned drones or eVTOL in Singapore and is flying.

      Verbatim
      I am the founder of an eVTOL company that designs manned drones or eVTOL in Singapore and is flying.

    • Dr Neo said he would explore the emerging high-growth market, set out opportunities and challenges for Singapore, and propose strategies and initiatives for building an eVTOL industry.

      Verbatim
      I will explore this emerging and high-growth market, dissect the opportunities and challenges that we face in Singapore and propose some strategies and also what initiatives that we can have into building an eVTOL industry going forward.

    • Dr Neo said he uses the term low-altitude economy because he finds it more encompassing than advanced air mobility.

      Verbatim
      I actually find that the low-altitude economy is more encompassing and that is why I use the terminology low-altitude economy.

    • Dr Neo said the eVTOL commercial market is projected to reach $216 billion by 2035, with a compounded annual growth rate of 51.8%.

      Verbatim
      It is projected to reach $216 billion by 2035, with a compounded annual growth rate of 51.8%.

    • Dr Neo said Singapore could look at regional air mobility, bringing people between places such as Singapore and Johor, and Singapore and Batam.

      Verbatim
      we can look at the air mobility business, that is, bringing people from one place to another on a regional side – Singapore and Johor, Singapore and Batam, a regional pathway that we can hop from one place to another.

    • Dr Neo said NTU's eVTOL had done its initial hover test in Singapore, but the flight trials had to be conducted in Germany.

      Verbatim
      the trials had to be conducted in Germany forthe flight.

    • Dr Neo proposed a national initiative involving a triple helix of Government, industry, and research institutes and universities.

      Verbatim
      We first need to have a national initiative involving a triple helix of Government, industry and of course, the research institutes and universities.

    • Dr Neo said Singapore should have a national strategy for the low-altitude economy.

      Verbatim
      We should have a strategy, Mr Deputy Speaker, a national strategy for low-altitude economy.

    • Dr Neo said there is currently no specialisation in low-altitude mobility or advanced air mobility technology in Singapore.

      Verbatim
      Currently, there is no specialisation in such low-altitude mobility or advanced air mobility technology in Singapore.

    • Dr Neo proposed getting out of Singapore to have a regional sandbox.

      Verbatim
      we should get out of Singapore, and therefore have a regional sandbox.

    • Dr Neo recommended that the National Research Foundation consider this a white space and allocate money for the industry, universities and research institutions.

      Verbatim
      I would recommend that the National Research Foundation consider this to be a white space and really aggressively allocate some good money for the industry, and the universities and research institutions.

    • Dr Neo said Singapore does not design and build aircraft but has attained 10% of the world's MRO market.

      Verbatim
      Singapore does not design and build aircraft, but we have attained 10% of the world's MRO market.

  • Ms Sun Xueling

    • Ms Sun said the Government pays close attention to the development of the low-altitude economy.

      Verbatim
      The Government pays close attention to the development of the low-altitude economy.

    • Ms Sun said it may not be viable to deploy eVTOLs extensively as a domestic transport option.

      Verbatim
      Unfortunately, it may not be viable to deploy eVTOLs extensively as a domestic transport option.

    • Ms Sun said eVTOLs could eventually become viable for cross-border travel to adjacent offshore islands or cross-border cargo transfer with neighbouring countries.

      Verbatim
      However, eVTOLs could eventually become a viable option for cross-border travel to adjacent offshore islands, or even cross-border cargo transfer with neighbouring countries.

    • Ms Sun said BCA and HDB already use drones to conduct periodic façade inspections faster and more efficiently.

      Verbatim
      For the built environment, the Building and Construction Authority, and the Housing and Development Board already use drones to conduct periodic façade inspections in a faster and more efficient manner.

    • Ms Sun said using drones to monitor water quality and activities at reservoirs can potentially reduce required man-hours by up to 70%.

      Verbatim
      Using drones in this manner can potentially reduce the required man-hours by up to 70%.

    • Ms Sun said CAAS facilitated initial hover tests of NTU's prototype eVTOL at the former Turf City racecourse in Kranji last year, ahead of its public unveiling at this year's Singapore Airshow.

      Verbatim
      CAAS facilitated the initial hover tests of their prototype eVTOL at the former Turf City racecourse in Kranji last year, ahead of its public unveiling at this year’s Singapore Airshow.

    • Ms Sun said the Government will review how to expand testing sites, including exploring overseas sandboxes with regional neighbours.

      Verbatim
      We will review how we can expand testing sites, including exploring overseas sandboxes in partnership with regional neighbours, as Dr Neo has suggested.

    • Ms Sun said in 2025 Singapore allowed some commercial drone operations at higher altitudes in designated areas for all days of the week for façade inspections.

      Verbatim
      In 2025, we allowed some commercial drone operations to be conducted at higher altitudes in designated areas for all days of the week for façade inspections.

    • Ms Sun said four out of five polytechnics are approved as Unmanned Aircraft Training Organisations and conduct practical drone operations courses.

      Verbatim
      Four out of our five polytechnics are also approved as Unmanned Aircraft Training Organisations, and conduct practical courses in drone operations.

    • Ms Sun said Singapore's airspace is limited.

      Verbatim
      First, Singapore’s airspace is limited.

    • Ms Sun said the Government has generally adopted a conservative approach in the past.

      Verbatim
      Against this backdrop, we have generally adopted a conservative approach in the past.

    • Ms Sun said the Government is studying overseas jurisdictions and will adapt what is relevant to Singapore's operating environment.

      Verbatim
      We are studying the approaches in overseas jurisdictions and will adapt what is relevant to Singapore’s operating environment.

    • Ms Sun said Chinese cities are trialling drones for uses including food and parcel deliveries, high-rise façade inspections, traffic monitoring and enforcement, and search and rescue, many of which Singapore may wish to explore.

      Verbatim
      Chinese cities are trialling drones for a multitude of urban use cases, including food and parcel deliveries, high-rise façade inspections, traffic monitoring and enforcement, and search and rescue operations, many of which Singapore may also wish to explore.

    • Ms Sun said the Government agrees with Dr Neo on bringing together the wider ecosystem and will consult all stakeholders.

      Verbatim
      We agree with Dr Neo that it is important to bring together the wider ecosystem and we will consult all stakeholders.

    • Ms Sun said the Ministry of Transport's immediate focus is to drive drone usage more extensively, especially by the public sector.

      Verbatim
      The Ministry of Transport's immediate focus is to drive the usage of drones more extensively, especially by the public sector and this is because we already have many potential use cases.

What happens next The House was adjourned without question put at 6.05 pm, pursuant to the Standing Order.

Open questions from this debate (7)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • Whether the Government will adopt a national strategy for the low-altitude economy, and if so, what form it would take.
  • Whether a dedicated sandbox or regional sandbox will be established, and where it would be located.
  • Whether new diploma or degree specialisations in low-altitude mobility will be introduced, and when.
  • Whether eVTOLs will be approved for cross-border passenger travel or cargo transfer, and under what conditions.
  • How potential safety, privacy and security issues from drone and eVTOL operations in dense urban areas would be addressed.
  • What funding, if any, the National Research Foundation might allocate to low-altitude economy research.
  • Whether regulations will be further changed to allow beyond-visual-line-of-sight operations or higher-altitude flights more broadly.

How this page was made

Built from the official Hansard record (Parliament of Singapore Official Reports). No news reporting was used. Briefs are written by software from the transcript and every key point carries the verbatim words it was drawn from.

  • Reports collected: 141 (complete)
  • Briefs on this page: 3 (158 verified points)
  • Speaker attribution: 97% of turns carry an explicit speaker tag
  • Any point whose quote could not be found in the transcript was discarded rather than shown.
